skill: Use Gaussian elimination on a singular two-equation, two-variable system; distinguish a contradictory final row from a redundant row and select the complete general solution.
reasoning_steps: Translate two equations into an augmented matrix.
Normalize the first x pivot when needed; eliminate the second x entry.
Interpret [0,0,d]: d nonzero means no solution; d=0 leaves y free and x=c/a-(b/a)y.
Select one of five radio answers, including No solution and four vector-form distractors.
invariants: Singular rank-one coefficient matrix, nonzero first x pivot; two variables x,y.
Easy examples have first x coefficient 1 and only one elimination operation; moderate examples normalize that pivot.
Both inconsistent and dependent consistent outcomes are essential: lesson tutorials 3153,3901,3154 explicitly distinguish these.
Response is radio selection with full general solution, not a free-entry row-reduction response.
permitted_variations: Vary first-row y coefficient and constant, including zero constant, and second-row nonzero multiplier; derive singular coefficients.
Independently vary consistency by changing second RHS relative to its row multiplier. Neither sign nor multiplier is a reason to fix consistency.
Vary the signs and magnitudes of the surviving affine solution; preserve single free variable y and x-first pivot for conservative same-method easy practice.

Vary answer order and plausible distractor profiles, including swapped coefficients, sign errors, shifted intercepts, and wrong second coordinates; preserve all observed complete banks at source replay.
